Identity
Every object or array has an
identity
: the order number in which it was created during the run. The first is 1, the next 2, and so on. Identity never changes and is never reused, even after the object is no longer used.
between objects compares identities: that is why
is
even though they hold the same data.
Reference cycles —an object pointing to another that points back to the first— are valid.

points.text: Primitives and texts are copied; objects are shared.
creates a new object and copies a single level.
Identity is the creation order and is never reused.
between objects compares identity, not contents.
